samples.summary: getStore() proxy guards only `setPageSetup` — every other DocStore mutator is still handed out unguarded, so read-only is still bypassable through the same handle
samples.evidence: The new proxy (editor.ts:2899-2915) intercepts exactly one member: `if (prop === 'setPageSetup') return guardedSetPageSetup;`. Every other property falls through to `Reflect.get(target, prop)` and is returned *bound to the real store* (line 2906). `DocStore` (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:11-146) exposes `setDocument`, `replaceDocument`, `updateBlock`, `insertBlock`, `deleteBlock`, `insertText`, `deleteText`, `applyStyle`, `applyBlockStyle`, `setBlockType`, `setHeader`/`setFooter`, `undo`/`redo`, and the whole table-op family — none of which honour `readOnly`. Attack: a viewer-role user (share link with `role !== 'editor'`, docs-view.tsx:327 passes `readOnly`) opens devtools or any first-party code path holding the `EditorAPI` and calls `editor.getStore().insertText('b1', 0, 'x')` / `.setDocument(evilDoc)`; the readOnly allowlist at editor.ts:3959-3981 neuters `api.setPageSetup` but nothing on the store, and the CRDT write reaches every collaborator. Server-side enforcement exists (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200 denies `rw` for non-editor share links) but is disabled unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (line 86-88, shadow mode returns allow), so in the default configuration the client guard is the only barrier. The risk of this shape of partial guard is that the surrounding comment ("the store `EditorAPI.getStore()` hands out", "one of that store's writes is the only one the editor guards") makes the handle read as covered when 40+ mutators are not.

samples.summary: `getDoc()` hands out the Doc wrapper (and, via TS-only `private store`, the raw unproxied DocStore), which walks around both the new getStore() guard and read-only
samples.evidence: `getDoc: () => doc` (editor.ts:2919) returns the `Doc` instance unmodified. `Doc` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:97) is a full mutation surface — `insertText` (261), `deleteText` (278), `deleteBlock` (628), `updateBlock` (644), `applyStyle` (409), `insertBlock` (652), table ops (849-933) — none of which consult `readOnly`. Worse for the new guard specifically: `private store: DocStore` (document.ts:98) is TypeScript-private only, so `(editor.getDoc() as any).store.setPageSetup(closedSetup)` reaches the *raw* `docStore`, not `guardedStore`, and persists exactly the closed content box the proxy was added to prevent — in read-only too. So the invariant the diff claims to move onto the editor is enforced on one of at least three public handles to the same store.

samples.summary: Proxy escape: `getPrototypeOf`/`defineProperty` are not trapped, so the raw `setPageSetup` can be extracted from the prototype and invoked with the proxy as `this`
samples.evidence: The handler defines only `get` and `set` (editor.ts:2900-2914). `Object.getPrototypeOf(editor.getStore())` is untrapped and returns `MemDocStore.prototype` / `YorkieDocStore.prototype`; `Object.getPrototypeOf(s).setPageSetup.call(s, {paperSize:{width:816,height:0},margins:{top:0,bottom:0,left:816,right:0}})` runs the real implementation with the proxy as receiver, whose internal property reads/writes forward through the (permissive) `get`/`set` traps to the real store — so `assertUsablePageSetup` and the `if (readOnly) return` at line 2895 are both skipped and the unusable geometry lands in the CRDT. `defineProperty` is likewise untrapped: `Object.defineProperty(editor.getStore(), 'setPageSetup', {value: f})` installs `f` on the underlying store, which the editor's own `writePageSetup` (line 2086) then calls. The `set` trap alone (line 2912) therefore does not make the guard tamper-proof; a `Proxy` used as a security boundary needs `getPrototypeOf`, `defineProperty` and `deleteProperty` trapped as well, or the guard belongs on the store implementation rather than on a wrapper.

samples.summary: No test or mechanism keeps the getStore() guard in sync with future mutating store methods, unlike the readOnly allowlist which at least documents that obligation
samples.evidence: The read-only path has an explicit allowlist with a 'keep this in sync' note (editor.ts:3956-3970); the new store proxy has no equivalent list and no test asserting that other mutators are blocked in read-only. The added tests only exercise `setPageSetup` (editor-read-only.test.ts:325-338, editor-page-setup.test.ts:329-350), so a suite that is green proves nothing about `getStore().setDocument()` or `getStore().insertText()` in a viewer session. Any store method added later is unguarded by default and nothing in the enforced lanes (tsc/eslint/vitest/knip) will notice.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The proxy at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2899-2915 intercepts only `setPageSetup` (line 2901); every other member resolves via `Reflect.get` and is returned bound to the real `docStore` (line 2906), and the `set` trap blocks only `setPageSetup` reassignment (2912). DocStore (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:11-147) declares ~40 mutators — setDocument (15), replaceDocument (21), insertBlock/deleteBlock (24-26), insertText/deleteText (72-74), applyStyle/applyStyles (76-97), setBlockType/applyBlockStyle (110-116), the table family (57-69), undo/redo (50-51) — none readOnly-aware. The read-only allowlist (editor.ts:3959-3981) neuters only EditorAPI methods and does not include `getStore`, which still hands out `guardedStore` (line 2920) in viewer sessions reached via docs-view.tsx:327. The documented authoritative backstop does deny `rw` for non-editor share links (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200) but is inert unless YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true' (86-88); otherwise handleAuth returns ALLOW/'shadow' (97-105), and packages/backend/README.md:111 documents the default as false. So no guard elsewhere makes the unguarded mutators unreachable, the code is present as described, and viewer-role write access is squarely in the authorization lane. No refutation ground applies.
